# Orientation — the 10-minute tour

`ticketd` is a small internal ticket tracker — a single Flask process backed by SQLite, in
production since 2019, doing ticket CRUD/lifecycle and a self-service password-reset flow, with
no login system of any kind protecting any of it. It's being rewritten on FastAPI + PostgreSQL
because of two known problems: notification emails are sent synchronously inside the request
(an SMTP hiccup can make ticket-closing itself hang or fail), and password-reset tokens are
generated with MD5 instead of a real random source. Everything else about its behavior — down
to a deliberate "return 200 with an empty object instead of 404" quirk the old UI depends on —
is being carried forward exactly unless a human explicitly rules otherwise.

- Legacy pinned at `tree-02fcc10` (unversioned-snapshot)
- Evidence subsystems: runtime_ingestion=inactive, data_census=inactive, trace_capture_t1=inactive

**Read this before trusting a confidence claim elsewhere in this guide.** This whole workspace
was generated with no access logs, no APM, and no production database access (contractor
handover, no git history), and non-interactively — no human was available to answer the six
open questions filed during generation (`decisions.md`'s "Still open" section). Every REPAIR
behavior's expected-divergence entry is currently **unratified**. None of that blocks the
workspace from existing; it does mean M0 can start today, but M1's gated work orders (WO-003,
WO-004) and all of M2 (WO-005) are waiting on a human, not on more agent work.
